primary.poolable_reason: THE ENDPOINTS AGREE AND THE MEASURE IS THE DEFECT -- WHICH MAKES THIS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER TOPIC IN THIS PASS. All three registrations read declare the same primary, verbatim: 'Percent Change From Baseline in Fasting Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) at Week 12'. THAT IS A CONTINUOUS QUANTITY. IT HAS NO EVENTS. An odds ratio requires a 2x2 table of participants who did and did not experience something, and a percent change in a laboratory value produces no such table. This page derived one anyway. WHAT THE COUNTS ACTUALLY ARE IS NOT RECORDED, AND THEIR MAGNITUDE SHOWS THEY ARE NOT EVENTS: SPIRE-LDL is stored as 971 in 1,068 placebo participants -- 91 per cent -- which is a threshold or responder flag of some kind, applied to an endpoint whose registered form is a mean change. Deriving an odds ratio from an undocumented dichotomisation of a continuous outcome discards the effect size the trials were designed to estimate and replaces it with a quantity that depends entirely on where the unrecorded threshold was placed.

pooled.withdrawn_note: WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: NOT that bococizumab does not lower LDL cholesterol -- it does, substantially, and these trials were designed to measure by how much. The trials here measure a mean percent change in LDL-C, a continuous quantity, and nothing on this page estimates the question its title implies. WHAT IS CONFIRMED: the original withdrawal was RIGHT and its one-line reason -- 'odds ratio on a continuous LDL-C endpoint' -- is precisely correct, which re-verification establishes rather than assumes. All trial identities are correct and all three registered primaries are the same endpoint. THE REPLACEMENT QUESTION IS AVAILABLE AND PARKED: these trials share an estimand exactly, so a MEAN DIFFERENCE synthesis is genuinely defensible -- it needs each trial's least-squares mean difference read from its results record, which is a source-document step this pass did not take.
pooled.reverification: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-18. VERDICT: CONFIRMED. The stated reason is exactly right and is now sourced: three registrations, one shared continuous primary, quoted verbatim. Re-verification added that the stored counts imply a 91-per-cent 'event' rate, showing they are an undocumented dichotomisation rather than events.
pooled.card_note: CONFIRMED: all three registrations declare the SAME continuous primary -- percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- and a continuous endpoint has no events for an odds ratio to be built from. The stored counts imply a 91% 'event' rate in placebo, so they are an undocumented dichotomisation. A MEAN DIFFERENCE synthesis here is defensible and is the parked replacement
